inputs.description: Cloud account owning the resource. Pick your own AWS account in NudgeBee.

CloudWatch namespace. AWS/EC2 for CPUUtilization, NetworkOut, NetworkIn, DiskReadBytes, DiskWriteBytes, StatusCheckFailed. CWAgent for MemoryUtilization, DiskUtilization and anything else the CloudWatch agent publishes.
Metric that alarmed, e.g. CPUUtilization, MemoryUtilization, DiskUtilization, NetworkOut, StatusCheckFailed.

ISO8601 UTC start of the window, e.g. 2026-09-03T12:00:00Z. Set this earlier than the alarm if you want to see what preceded it - the tool returns exactly the window you ask for and nothing outside it.
ISO8601 UTC end of the window, e.g. 2026-09-03T12:30:00Z.

What to read from the host. Default triage (load, top CPU/memory processes, disk, boot time). Others: top_cpu, top_memory, shell_history, cron_jobs, recent_logins, running_services, failed_services, network_connections, disk_usage, memory_usage, recent_syslog, process_tree, boot_time, package_changes. All read-only.

params.command: aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace {{ Inputs.namespace }} --metric-name {{ Inputs.metric_name }} --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value={{ Inputs.instance_id }} --start-time {{ Inputs.window_start }} --end-time {{ Inputs.window_end }} --period 60 --statistics Average Maximum --region {{ Inputs.region }} --output json

aws ssm list-commands --instance-id {{ Inputs.instance_id }} --filters key=InvokedAfter,value={{ Inputs.window_start }} key=InvokedBefore,value={{ Inputs.window_end }} --max-results 50 --region {{ Inputs.region }} --output json

llm_description:
Returns CloudWatch datapoints, SSM Run Command history and a read-only host inspection for one EC2 instance over a time window.

This is a data tool. It fetches and returns; it does not interpret. There is no verdict and no root cause - every SSM command in the window is returned in time order with its text, comment, status and timestamp, alongside the metric datapoints and live host state. Deciding what caused what is your job, not the tool's.

Set namespace and metric_name to whatever you want to look at: AWS/EC2 for CPUUtilization, NetworkOut, NetworkIn, StatusCheckFailed, DiskReadBytes, DiskWriteBytes; CWAgent for MemoryUtilization and DiskUtilization. Widen window_start beyond the alarm to see what preceded it.

host_action chooses what is read from the host - default triage; also top_cpu, top_memory, shell_history, cron_jobs, recent_logins, running_services, failed_services, network_connections, disk_usage, memory_usage, recent_syslog, process_tree, boot_time, package_changes.

Two things the data cannot tell you, which matter when reading it: SSH sessions, cron jobs and boot-time processes leave no trace in SSM history, and host inspection is a snapshot taken now, so a short-lived process may already be gone. An empty result is not evidence of absence.

The instance must be SSM-managed and online. Read-only: it never kills, restarts or reconfigures anything.
